title: Holder verification lockout per policy, atomic (S5-WFL-04 gate mediums)
story: As a carrier I want policy-holder verification to resist scripted guessing across sessions and parallel requests so that last name and ZIP cannot be brute-forced
acceptance: Failed verifications are counted per (tenant, policy number) in a module-owned table (migration in intake/index.mjs), not on the session, with a rolling window (e.g. 10 failures per 15 minutes per policy locks that policy's verification for the window); starting new sessions does not reset it (test)

The count is incremented atomically in one SQL statement before the coverage lookup result is revealed, so N parallel wrong guesses on one session or across sessions record N failures (test fires 20 concurrent wrong guesses and asserts the lock holds and the count is >= 20 or capped consistently)
Locked responses are the same uniform 404 as any other failure; a correct guess during lockout also gets 404 (test)
Per-session 5-attempt limit from S5-WFL-04 kept; CSR and agent rules unchanged; node --test tests/unit/intake/ passes; full npm test no new failures
brief: Findings from the S5-WFL-04 security gate: the lockout counter lives on the session document (bypass by new sessions) and is read-await-write (race). Use ctx.db (tenant-scoped) with an UPSERT ... SET failures = failures + 1 RETURNING failures, or an equivalent single statement. Store a keyed hash of the policy number (use ctx.crypto blind index or HMAC helper if one exists), not the plain number.
